open.name: Open
open.meaning: Tickets not yet closed in the selected period
open.formula: Count where status is not closed. PTR and PTR with permission count as closed.
open.source: Redmine issues mirrored into the dashboard, filtered like the table

closed.name: Closed
closed.meaning: Tickets closed in Redmine, or in a status the business treats as closed
closed.redmineOnly: the statuses Redmine marks as closed
closed.source: Redmine issue status, with the dashboard's closed-status list

breached.name: Breached
breached.meaning: Tickets whose age passed their SLA, including tickets that closed late
breached.formula: Age in days > SLA days. Age stops at close date, then Redmine close time, then last status change.
breached.source: SLA days by priority from the dashboard's SLA policy

atRisk.name: At risk
atRisk.meaning: Open tickets close to breaching their SLA
atRisk.formula: Open, not breached, and days left ≤ cushion. Cushion: {cushions}
atRisk.source: SLA days and cushions by priority from the dashboard's SLA policy

mttrWorkaround.name: MTTR (workaround)
mttrWorkaround.meaning: Average days from a ticket being created to a workaround being in place
mttrWorkaround.formula: Average of (resolution date − created date) in whole days, over tickets that have a resolution date. Rounded to 2 decimals.

mttrPermanent.name: MTTR (permanent)
mttrPermanent.meaning: Average days from a ticket being created to its permanent fix
mttrPermanent.formula: Average of (close date − created date) in whole days, over tickets that have a close date. Rounded to 2 decimals.

workaroundDebt.name: Workaround debt
workaroundDebt.meaning: Tickets running on a workaround that still have no permanent fix
workaroundDebt.formula: Count where a resolution date is set and the close date is empty
workaroundDebt.source: Redmine custom fields: resolution date and close date

trend.name: Created / Closed
trend.meaning: How many tickets were opened and closed in each period
trend.formula: Created counts by creation date. Closed counts by the day the clock stopped: {rule}.
trend.source: Redmine issues mirrored into the dashboard

topCategories.name: Top categories
topCategories.meaning: The incident categories with the most tickets in the selected period
topCategories.formula: Count per category, highest first. Tickets without a category count as Unclassified. The change compares with the preceding period of the same length.

matrix.name: Impact × Urgency
matrix.meaning: How tickets spread across impact and urgency severity
matrix.formula: Count per impact and urgency pair. Unclassified means the field is empty; Unknown means the value has no matching label. Colours follow the SPO impact and urgency matrix; the SLA still follows each ticket's recorded priority.
matrix.source: Redmine custom fields: impact severity and urgency severity

slaBuckets.name: SLA buckets
slaBuckets.meaning: Share of SLA time used, for all tickets. Different from At risk, which counts open tickets only.
slaBuckets.formula: Age in days ÷ SLA days, grouped as 0-50%, 50-80%, 80-100% and Breached. Unknown when the age cannot be worked out.
slaBuckets.source: SLA days by priority from the dashboard's SLA policy

freshness.name: Data freshness
freshness.meaning: How recently the dashboard copied data from Redmine
freshness.formula: The mirror refreshes about every {minutes} minutes. Data is stale when no refresh has finished within four intervals, or the copy lags Redmine by more than an hour.

aging.name: Aging
aging.meaning: How many days a ticket has been in progress, next to its SLA days
aging.formula: Calendar days from creation to the day the clock stopped ({rule}), or to today while the ticket is open
aging.source: Redmine issues mirrored into the dashboard

slaColumn.name: SLA
slaColumn.meaning: Where a ticket stands against its SLA
slaColumn.formula: Age in days ÷ SLA days for the ticket's priority, shown as 0-50%, 50-80%, 80-100% or Breached
slaColumn.source: SLA days by priority from the dashboard's SLA policy

noRedmine.name: No Redmine
noRedmine.meaning: Redmine ticket number; opens the ticket in Redmine

slaCompliance.name: SLA compliance
slaCompliance.meaning: Share of tickets closed this year that were closed within their SLA
slaCompliance.formula: Closed tickets that did not breach, divided by all closed tickets, as a percentage. Empty when nothing has closed.
slaCompliance.source: SLA days by priority from the dashboard SLA policy, over the incidents closed from 1 January

groupCounts.name: Ticket groups
groupCounts.meaning: Open and breached tickets for each group: Incident, Problem and Service Request
groupCounts.formula: Per group, open plus closed equals total. Breached is the open and closed tickets whose age passed their SLA.
groupCounts.source: Redmine trackers grouped by the dashboard tracker scope configuration

matrixMissing.name: Missing impact or urgency
matrixMissing.meaning: Tickets that cannot be placed in the matrix because impact or urgency was left blank
matrixMissing.formula: Count of tickets in the current filters where impact or urgency has no value. The link opens exactly these tickets.
matrixMissing.source: Redmine custom fields: impact severity and urgency severity

avgResolution.name: Average resolution
avgResolution.meaning: How many days a closed incident took on average, from creation to close
avgResolution.formula: Mean age in days of closed incidents from 1 January. Age stops at close date, then Redmine close time, then last status change.
avgResolution.source: Redmine issue dates and status history

mttr.name: MTTR
mttr.meaning: Average days a closed ticket took, from creation to close
mttr.formula: Mean of (close date − created date) in days over the closed tickets in the current filters. Clicking the tile lists exactly those tickets.
mttr.source: Redmine issue dates; close date, then Redmine close time, then last status change

dashboard.openInList: Open these filters in the incident list

forecast.note: A statistical projection of daily created tickets from the last 180 days: a weekday pattern plus a linear trend, with a 95% range. It does not know about releases, outages or holidays — treat it as a baseline, not a promise.

rec.STABLE: Forecast is stable and within the normal range.
rec.SURGE: Volume is expected to rise 30% or more — consider extra cover.
rec.DROP: Volume is expected to fall 30% or more.
rec.HIGH_RISK_DAY: At least one forecast day is well above the recent average.

forecast.chartSub: Blue: history. Orange: forecast. Shaded: 95% range.
forecast.mapeNote: MAPE is the mean absolute percentage error of a backtest over the last 7 days. Under 20% is good, 20–40% fair, over 40% poor.
forecast.seasonalitySub: Volume relative to the daily average: above 1× is busier, below is quieter.

alerts.allClear: No active alerts for this ticket group.

DATA_STALE.title: Data is stale
DATA_STALE.rule: The mirror has not refreshed within its expected interval; figures may be behind Redmine.

BREACHED_OPEN.title: Open tickets past SLA
BREACHED_OPEN.rule: Open tickets whose age exceeds their SLA target. Worst first.

AT_RISK.title: Tickets at risk of breaching
AT_RISK.rule: Open tickets with no more days left than their priority's cushion.

CRITICAL_HIGH_OPEN.title: Critical and High tickets still open
CRITICAL_HIGH_OPEN.rule: Every open ticket with Critical or High priority.

FORECAST_SURGE.title: Volume surge forecast
FORECAST_SURGE.rule: The forecast expects 30% or more tickets than the last 7 days. See Forecast.

rca.worklist: Open problems without a root cause

sla.note: The policy every SLA figure in this dashboard is computed with, read live from configuration. Administrators change it on the Parameters page, and the numbers re-derive on the next mart refresh.
sla.ladderSub: Days allowed to resolve, and the at-risk cushion (days left at which an open ticket is flagged).
sla.closeRuleSub: First rule that has a value wins.
sla.closedByOverrideSub: Statuses Redmine leaves open that the business treats as closed.

ai.privacy: Everything here is computed on the dashboard server from the same data as the other pages; no ticket text is sent anywhere unless an administrator has configured an AI provider, in which case the card says so.

summary.title: Daily summary
summary.sub: What happened on a day, and what needs attention now.

ai.local: Computed locally — no external AI provider configured.
ai.provider: Briefing written by {name}; the figures are computed locally.

qa.title: Ask a question
qa.sub: Answers a defined set of questions about the filtered tickets and says when it cannot.
qa.placeholder: e.g. What is the average aging of BNI incidents?
qa.notUnderstood: I can answer questions about counts, open/closed, SLA compliance, breaches, MTTR, aging and closure rate — optionally for one institusi, priority, source or assignee. Try:
qa.q1: What is the average aging of BNI incidents?
qa.q3: What is the SLA compliance for external tickets?

search.title: Ticket search
search.sub: Ranks tickets by word relevance (TF-IDF) over subject, category and institusi. It matches words, not meaning.
search.none: No ticket shares a word with that query.

patterns.title: Recurring patterns
patterns.sub: Same institusi and category at least 3 times in the period.
patterns.none: No recurring pattern in this period.
patterns.workaroundOf: {w} closed on a workaround · {perm} with a permanent fix

rec.PERMANENT_FIX: Closed on workarounds but it keeps coming back — plan a permanent fix.
rec.DOCUMENT_ROOT_CAUSE: Most occurrences have no root cause — analyse and document it.

placeholder.title: AI Insights — coming soon
placeholder.body: The AI provider has not been chosen yet, so this page is a placeholder.

params.title: Parameters
params.note: Everything the dashboard treats as a rule rather than a fact: SLA budgets, when an alert fires, and the forecast and brand-network settings. Changes apply on the next page load; SLA changes re-derive the numbers on the next mart refresh. Every change is logged.
params.readOnly: You can view these settings but not change them.

sla.title: SLA by priority
sla.sub: Days allowed to resolve a ticket, and the at-risk cushion (days left at which an open ticket is flagged). A higher priority cannot get a longer budget than a lower one.

alerts.title: Alert rules
alerts.sub: When each alert fires on the Alerts page. A rule fires only when at least the minimum number of tickets match.

thresholdHint.BREACHED_OPEN: Escalate to Critical when this many High/Critical tickets are breached (0 = never)
thresholdHint.UNASSIGNED_OPEN: Only count tickets open at least this many days (0 = all)
thresholdHint.AGING_OPEN: Open tickets older than this many days

general.title: Forecast and brand network
general.sub: Scalar settings used by the Forecast, Alerts and Category pages.

param.forecast_surge_change_pct: Surge alert when next period grows by (%)
